followup: Seek an existing cluster test or source-backed I/O fault that yields a follower currentEpoch/lastZxid ahead of the leader and still reaches the selected comparison; do not repeat the after-setAcceptedEpoch IOException plan.
scope: One existing QuorumRestartTest rolling-restart JUnit and one precise after-setAcceptedEpoch IOException pilot; other workloads and fault models remain untested.
source_findings: In Learner.registerWithLeader, newEpoch > acceptedEpoch encodes currentEpoch into ACKEPOCH, then setAcceptedEpoch writes acceptedEpoch to disk before the precise injected write door; an equal-epoch retry encodes -1 instead.

Leader.waitForEpochAck returns if electionFinished and evaluates the selected isMoreRecentThan comparison only when StateSummary.currentEpoch != -1. The pilot trace shows the retried packet entered this method and exited without the selected TARGET_CHECK; it does not record the ACK payload, so the -1 route is source-grounded rather than directly observed.

An IOException at the earlier FOLLOWERINFO write or LEADERINFO read aborts registerWithLeader before setAcceptedEpoch; retry can retain the guard, but those operations do not increase follower currentEpoch or lastLoggedZxid relative to leaderStateSummary in this existing rolling-restart test.

AcceptedEpoch persistence changes the protocol epoch handshake but is not an operand in StateSummary.isMoreRecentThan. The present exact-door model has no demonstrated path that both influences currentEpoch/zxid and retains the selected guard.
